svg.text: FOXBODY BCM - SENSORS / ANALOG / COMMUNICATIONS
BCM owns body sensing and fuel level. MicroSquirt remains engine-management authority and supplies engine data digitally.
ANALOG BOARD
Protected ADC/front-end - exact module to freeze
A0 Fuel sender
A1 Battery current
A2 Driver window current
A3 Passenger window current
A4 Fan 1 current
A5 Fan 2 current
A6 Battery voltage (protected)
A7 Spare / pressure transducer
ADC digital bus -> BCM Controller
DIGITAL SENSORS
Cabin temperature/humidity -> I2C / 1-Wire
Ambient temperature -> 1-Wire
Ambient light -> I2C
Rain sensor -> final automotive optical interface
IMU -> I2C/SPI for impact, tilt, jack/tow detection
TPMS receiver -> serial/USB/RF interface
BCM enclosure temp -> digital sensor
Bluetooth phone proximity -> BCM Controller radio
GPS/cellular hotspot = future optional hardware
COMMUNICATIONS
Input Board -> isolated RS485 adapter -> USB -> BCM Controller
MicroSquirt -> serial/CAN-compatible interface as finalized -> BCM/Dash
BCM Controller <-> FoxbodyDash over local network/API
LIN Adapter reserved for future LIN devices
I/O Expander (MCP23017) supplies low-voltage GPIO only.
Never connect raw automotive +12V to MCP23017 pins.
FUEL LEVEL
Factory tank sender -> protected excitation / measurement network -> Analog Board A0.
Calibration routine: record near-empty, then known added gallons at multiple points.
Recommended calibration points: near empty, ~2 gal, 5 gal, 10 gal, 15 gal, full.
BCM stores lookup table and filters fuel slosh before publishing fuel %/gallons.
Future upgrade can change sender technology without changing dash/API architecture.
SENSOR / POWER RULES
F23 SENSOR / ANALOG SUPPLY - 5A from BCM electronics bus.
Use regulated 5V/3.3V rails where sensors require them; do not power sensors from random GPIO.
Analog automotive inputs require transient protection and voltage scaling before ADC.
Hall current sensors are sized to the load: windows, battery, and fans may use different ranges.
Sensor grounds return to the documented electronics ground, not motor-current return paths.
Shield/twisted-pair usage is assigned per sensor/bus; shield drains are not grounded randomly.
TPMS = four wheel sensors plus receiver; individual pressure/temp is published to the dash.
BCM ELECTRONICS GROUND BUS
Analog Board selection is intentionally the remaining sensor-interface hardware decision; channel count and automotive input protection are now defined before purchase.
